body.statement: Every finite linear program with binary-encoded rational coefficients can be solved by an exact algorithm whose running time is polynomial in the total input encoding length: the algorithm decides feasibility and, when the feasible objective is bounded, returns an exact rational optimal value and an exact rational optimal solution.

source.locator: Lecture 5, Section 2.4 (Polynomial Time Algorithms for Linear Programming)

attestation.note: The cited section states polynomial-time solvability of linear programming and explains exact recovery from the polynomial-bit rational coordinates of an optimum.
